cohort: Teenage pregnancies (<=19 years) at Saveetha Medical College and Hospital between 2011-2019.
finding: Teenage pregnancies had a higher incidence of vaginal delivery (82%), but also experienced more complications (anemia, postpartum hemorrhage, premature rupture of membranes, placenta previa, abruption, neonatal death, IUGR in 27% of cases and inadequate weight gain and failure to thrive in 43% of cases) compared to adult pregnancies.
mod_finding: While 82% of teenage pregnancies resulted in vaginal delivery, 14% were Cesarean and 4% forceps deliveries, with no significant association found between mode of delivery and teenage pregnancy.
